The '''corsit-puzzle tree''' was a type of [[Tree/Legends|tree]] that grew on [[Thonner/Legends|Thonner]],<ref name="Tessent" /> a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> It could be found in the [[Swamp/Legends|marshlands]] of the [[Lesser Firagh Peninsula]] of Thonner's [[Firagh]] continent, an area rife with dangerous wildlife. The trunk of the corsit-puzzle tree was thickly covered with spikes, and the tree's name referred to the fact that not even [[corsit]]s, [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibious]] creatures that were expert climbers, could not scale its branches without impaling themselves in the process.<ref name="Tessent" />

Every few [[Standard month/Legends|months]], [[Thonnermen]], the inhabitants of Thonner, visited the Lesser Firagh Peninsula in order to harvest corsit-puzzle tree [[Wood/Legends|wood]]. They felled the trees using [[lasercutter]]s and used larger boughs and stumps to fashion pit traps for [[Hunting/Legends|catching]] large game. On smaller branches, Thonnermen used lasercutters to remove the spikes from a surface area sufficiently large to hold with [[Glove/Legends|ungloved]] [[Limb/Legends|hands]]. The resultant vicious [[Melee weapon/Legends|melee weapons]] were known as [[puzzle-wood staff]]s.<ref name="Tessent" />

==Behind the scenes==
The corsit-puzzle tree was introduced in the [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] adventure "[[Race for the Tessent]]," which was published for use with [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Tessent" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref>
